question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class agent-scoped web/tool credential contract here, and should the durable surface be `agents.list[].tools.web`, a generic per-agent plugin/tool config contract, or both?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but automation cannot safely choose credential precedence, SecretRef scope, redaction, plugin-owned config interaction, and upgrade semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a generic agent-scoped web/tool contract
options.body: Define one precedence and SecretRef contract covering `tools.web`, plugin-owned `webSearch`, docs, reload behavior, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Add only `agents.list[].tools.web`
options.body: This would address the narrow issue faster but risks creating a second credential source that drifts from plugin-owned web-search config.

options.title: Keep web credentials global
options.body: This preserves a lean config surface but leaves multi-agent billing, rate-limit, and credential isolation unresolved.

recommendation.title: Design a generic agent-scoped web/tool contract
recommendation.body: Define one precedence and SecretRef contract covering `tools.web`, plugin-owned `webSearch`, docs, reload behavior, and regression tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans config compatibility, SecretRef/security semantics, and web-search/plugin boundaries where the available history points most strongly to this owner.
